meta.title: dsh-connect-workbuddy
meta.description: Connects locally signed-in WorkBuddy models, CN and international alike, to DSH, reading each model's credit multiplier from the upstream catalog on every refresh, with per-model image input toggles, account switching backed by an auto-failing-over pool, manual daily check-in, and read-only credit overviews shown as compact pills on the card and in the composer.

en.composer.newModelsNote: "New" means this machine recorded the model id for the first time; it says nothing about when the upstream listed it. Only models first seen within the last 7 days are shown.
en.composer.newModelsRow: Models first seen by this machine
en.composer.newModelsTitle: Models first seen by this machine:
en.composer.testAllHint: Test every account in this region, one at a time
en.quotaNotice.fallbackHead: The quota for this request is exhausted
en.quotaNotice.supplement: (some models also have a daily limit that is unrelated to your credits)
en.row.accountsHint: Choose from locally detected sign-ins. Tokens are never shown or saved in DSH settings.
en.row.accountsWriteFailed: The account change was not saved: {message} — the active profile's configuration file could not be updated (on Windows it may be locked by an antivirus scanner or a sync client). Your previous choice is still in effect; close whatever holds that file and try again (see docs/WINDOWS.md in the plugin repo for the exact path).
en.row.cardCrashed: The configuration area failed to render.
en.row.cardCrashedHint: The model provider itself is unaffected — chat and credits keep working. Quote the line above in a bug report.
en.row.cliBridgeEffortAria: Reasoning effort the local CodeBuddy CLI runs on
en.row.cliBridgeEffortHint: Written to cliBridge.effort and passed to the CLI as --effort. "CLI default" leaves the tier to the CLI itself. When the picked model lists supported tiers, only those are offered.
en.row.cliBridgeHint: Adds the codebuddy_ask tool and the /codebuddy command. Each call spends CodeBuddy quota. injectResult only affects /codebuddy — its result is injected back into the session, costing one DSH turn when the session is idle; tool calls never read it. Rate-limited: 6 turns per session per hour, 20 per process per hour, one turn at a time. Off by default.
en.row.cliBridgeLabel: Let the local CodeBuddy CLI do the work
en.row.cliBridgeModelAria: Model the local CodeBuddy CLI runs on
en.row.cliBridgeModelHint: Written to cliBridge.model and passed to the CLI as --model. "CLI default" leaves the model to the CLI itself. The list is the catalog this tab synced from the upstream.
en.row.cliBridgePickersHint: All three pickers write the global cliBridge block; "CLI default" on model and effort is an explicit empty value, not "unset" — the CLI then uses its own defaults; the region picker writes cliBridge.regionOrder.
en.row.cliBridgeRegionOrderAria: Order in which the local CodeBuddy CLI walks the credential regions
en.row.cliBridgeRegionOrderHint: Written to cliBridge.regionOrder: the order the CLI tries the WorkBuddy credentials in, until one logs in. The region actually used is reported per turn as credential_region. Applies from the next call.
en.row.credentialRejectedChoose: Other local sign-ins exist but none of them answered the upstream just now. Try switching to one above; if none works, sign in again in the desktop app.
en.row.credentialRejectedIntro: The token for "{accountName}" is no longer accepted by the upstream, so credits and check-in are unavailable. Signing in again only helps if the problem is the token itself — here is what actually applies:
en.row.credentialRejectedRelogin: No other local sign-in exists to switch to. Sign in again in the WorkBuddy desktop app.
en.row.credentialRejectedSwitch: Another sign-in on this machine answered the upstream: "{accountName}". Switching to it fixes this — no need to sign in again.
en.row.creditPositionDisabledHint: Unavailable while the switch above is off: tick "Show credits in the composer toolbar" first.
en.row.creditPositionHint: Where the credit readout sits. "composer toolbar" is the default (the row with the model picker). Choose "below the input box" — the row carrying the round / step / token statistics — if another plugin occupies the composer toolbar and the readout does not appear.
en.row.creditPositionHintInline: Where the readout sits. "composer toolbar" is the default — the row with the model picker.
en.row.desc: Use WorkBuddy models in DSH: each refresh reads every model's credit multiplier from the upstream catalog, image input is toggled per model, several accounts can be switched or failed over automatically, and daily check-in plus your remaining credits are one click away. The domestic and international sides are two independent providers, each with its own account — use both at the same time.
en.row.diagHint: What this card actually read, so a report can quote it. Nothing here changes a setting.
en.row.imageToolHint: Adds the workbuddy_draw_image tool, which the MODEL may call on its own — about 5.71 credits per image on the CN gateway and about 0.03 on the international one, with no per-call confirmation. Ticking it here only authorizes THIS tab's region. Off everywhere means the tool is not registered at all.
en.row.keepPromptLastHint: Moves the harness-injected runtime context above your real prompt, so the usage page stops showing "Time sampled…" as your question. Message count and text are preserved. Off by default because it changes the message order the upstream counts.
en.row.keepPromptLastLabel: Record what you actually typed, not the injected context
en.row.mediaModelsEmpty: This region publishes no image or video model.
en.row.mediaModelsError: Could not read the media model list: {message}
en.row.mediaModelsHint: Read from this account's product configuration. The draw tool picks its model from here: a prompt without an image uses a text-to-image model, one WITH an image uses an image-to-image model. Read-only — to use a different model, pass it to the tool.
en.row.modelCapabilityPending: Only capabilities advertised by WorkBuddy are shown.
en.row.modelImageText: Image input: the vendor documents this model as text-only, so a refresh leaves it unchecked. Tick it yourself only if you know it reads images.
en.row.modelImageUnverified: Image input unverified: no vendor source confirms this model reads images, so a refresh leaves it unchecked rather than guessing. Tick it yourself if you have verified it works.
en.row.modelOffHint: Offer the “off” level for this model
en.row.modelOffRefusedHint: Measured to reject the “off” level with HTTP 400 (code 11133) on both gateways. With this ticked, every request that carries no reasoning tier — compaction summaries above all — would fail, so it cannot be enabled here.
en.row.modelsTestAllHint: Tests EVERY model in this region's catalog, including the ones you have NOT enabled — so it costs noticeably more than "test enabled models". Same per-probe cost, same early stop on a rejected credential.
en.row.modelsTestAuth: Stopped: the credential was rejected, so every remaining model would answer the same way. Sign in again, then re-run.
en.row.modelsTestEnabledHint: Tests every model you have ENABLED, one request each — each probe sends a real-volume request, so this spends real credit (about 0.01 per model at the default 25000-token size). Rows show their verdict as it lands. Stops early if the credential is rejected.
en.row.oauthDone: Added “{accountName}”. Pick it above to use it.
en.row.oauthExpires: The sign-in window expires in about {minutes} min.
en.row.oauthOpened: Opened. Waiting for you to finish…
en.row.oauthOpenHint: Open the sign-in page and confirm — the account is added here automatically when you finish:
en.row.oauthTimedOut: The sign-in timed out — start again when ready.
en.row.oauthTitle: Add an account by QR sign-in
en.row.oauthTitleGlobal: Add an account by web sign-in
en.row.oauthWaiting: Waiting for the sign-in to finish… ({seconds}s)
en.row.panelCapabilitiesHint: What the plugin may do on your behalf. Each switch takes effect on the click — there is no Save button in this section.
en.row.poolBenefitHint: Claim it on the plans page: {url}
en.row.poolBusyHint: Running one account at a time…
en.row.poolEnabledHint: On: the pool picks the account for every request, and only a failover-worthy failure moves to the next account — a malformed request, a busy model, a platform queue, or a channel-gate refusal does not (switching accounts would only burn quota for the same refusal). Off: the account you select serves every request, and a failure is reported as it is.
en.row.poolErrFailed: The batch failed on the host side: {message}
en.row.poolErrHttp: The batch was refused (HTTP {status}). Check the plugin is up to date and try again.
en.row.poolErrNoCheckin: This region has no daily check-in — the action is not offered here.
en.row.poolErrNoFreeModel: This region has no zero-multiplier model to test with. Refresh the model catalog, or pick a target model yourself.
en.row.poolErrNoLiveMembers: Every account checked into this pool has lost its local sign-in, so the batch had nothing to run. Sign in again in the WorkBuddy desktop app, or save to drop them.
en.row.poolErrNoMembers: No account is checked into this pool — the batch had nothing to run. Check at least one account and save.
en.row.poolErrRouteMissing: The batch endpoint did not answer (HTTP {status}, no body) — the DSH Host is probably still running older plugin code, so this route is not registered. Quit DSH completely and start it again, then retry.
en.row.poolErrStaleModel: The target model is no longer offered by this region. Pick another, or switch back to automatic.
en.row.poolErrUnavailable: The account pool is not available in this build (or its batch route is missing). Restart the app; if it persists, the plugin needs reinstalling.
en.row.poolGhostMembers: {count} pool member(s) are no longer signed in on this machine, so they are not counted and not used: {names}. Remove any you no longer need below.
en.row.poolGhostRemoveNamed: Remove {account} from this pool. This account is no longer signed in on this machine.
en.row.poolGhostRemoveUnnamed: Remove {account} from this pool. No name was ever recorded for this account, so what you see is the start of its id.
en.row.poolLogCheckinStart: Checking in {count} account(s), one at a time
en.row.poolLogEmpty: Nothing yet. Check-ins, tests, and account switches are recorded here.
en.row.poolLogTestDone: Test finished; the pool was re-ranked
en.row.poolLogTestRowMalformed: {accountName}: the host returned no result for this account
en.row.poolMembersHint: Only checked accounts rotate, get checked in, and get tested.
en.row.poolModelWideBusy: Every member is blocked on the same model — this is the model, not your accounts.
en.row.poolModelWideBusyHint: Switching accounts cannot help: the limit follows the model, so a different account hits the same wall. Wait about a minute, or switch to a less busy model in this session.
en.row.poolMoveDownAria: Move {accountName} down in this pool's order
en.row.poolMoveDownTitle: Move account down in this pool's order
en.row.poolMoveUpAria: Move {accountName} up in this pool's order
en.row.poolMoveUpTitle: Move account up in this pool's order
en.row.poolNoCandidate: No account in this pool can be used right now.
en.row.poolNoCandidateHint: Members are rate-limited, out of credits, rejected, or unreachable. Rate limits, drained quotas and transient failures return to the pool on their own — at the time the upstream states, or after a 30-minute fallback. Only a rejected credential needs a new sign-in.
en.row.poolNoneSelected: No account is checked into this pool.
en.row.poolNoneSelectedHint: Check at least one account to enable check-in and test.
en.row.poolNotMemberHint: Not in the pool: rotation skips it, and batch check-in and test leave it alone.
en.row.poolOrderBadgeNote: The badge shows the position you SAVED, not the live ranking. An account can read "No. 2" while being benched for a rate limit — the number is your saved preference, and the pool skips accounts it cannot bill right now.
en.row.poolOrderRuleExpiring: 2. Does it have credits expiring within 3 days? Yes goes first. This also outranks your manual order — see the note below.
en.row.poolOrderRuleExpiringAmount: 5. How many are expiring? Between those same accounts, the one with more at stake goes first. With nothing expiring this is equivalent to comparing totals.
en.row.poolOrderRuleFreshness: 7. Freshness of the sign-in. The more recently issued credential wins a draw.
en.row.poolOrderRuleId: 8. Account id. A final tie-break, so the same pool always produces the same order.
en.row.poolOrderRuleManual: 3. Your manual order. The position you set with the ↑ / ↓ arrows. Accounts you never ordered are placed after every ordered one.
en.row.poolOrderRuleNearestExpiry: 4. Which expiry comes first? Between accounts that both have credits expiring, the one losing them sooner goes first.
en.row.poolOrderRulesIntro: The pool always picks the first account that can actually be billed right now. The rules below are checked in order — the first one that separates two accounts decides; later rules only break ties.
en.row.poolOrderRulesTitle: How this pool chooses an account
en.row.poolOrderRuleTotal: 6. Total credits. The account holding more goes first, so a nearly-drained account is kept in reserve.
en.row.poolOrderRuleUsable: 1. Can it be billed right now? Accounts that are rate-limited, out of credit, credential-rejected, or failing are moved to the back until their cooldown ends. This outranks everything, including your own order below.
en.row.poolOrderWhy: Why expiring credits outrank your manual order: expiring credits are money about to disappear, while a manual order may be stale or set by accident. If the manual order won, one mis-drag could let credits lapse unused. So an account with credits expiring within 3 days always goes ahead of one without, even if you dragged it to the bottom.
en.row.poolProbeSizeHint: How much text a test sends. The upstream refuses a request once it grows past roughly 20K–30K tokens, so a test smaller than your real conversations answers "usable" for an account that would refuse them. Bigger tests are more truthful but cost more credit each.
en.row.poolRankAutoTitle: Not manually sorted yet: the pool spends expiring credits first, then picks accounts by remaining balance. Use ↑/↓ to set your own order.
en.row.poolRankManualTitle: You placed this account at position {rank} in the pool manually.
en.row.poolRegionNote: The domestic and international pools are fully independent: accounts, switches, intervals, and target models never affect each other.
en.row.poolRetryUnknown: The upstream gave no time for when this frees up
en.row.poolRowRemoved: {accountName}: hidden from the list. 「Detect accounts again」 re-adds it; the desktop app stays signed in.
en.row.poolRowRemoveDesktopOnly: {accountName}: hidden from the list — this account comes from the desktop app's own sign-in, which is left untouched. 「Detect accounts again」 re-adds it.
en.row.poolRowRemoveHint: Remove this account from the list. The WorkBuddy desktop app is not signed out — it keeps its own sign-in. Removing only hides the account here; 「Detect accounts again」 brings it back.
en.row.poolSavedStaleRefresh: Saved, but the panel could not re-read it. The value is stored; the next refresh will show it.
en.row.poolSelectAria: Include {accountName} in this region's account pool
en.row.poolServingOutside: “{account}” is serving right now but is not in this pool: rotation will not pick it, and batch check-in and test will not touch it.
en.row.poolSettingsHint: These are preferences: they take effect when you save (same as the model list). Test results are written automatically and are not affected by this button.
en.row.poolTargetHint: One model for every account here — the test measures each row with it. Auto picks a zero-multiplier model from this region's catalog, preferring the largest context window; a manual choice wins.
en.row.poolTargetNone: This region has no zero-multiplier model yet.
en.row.poolTargetNoneHint: The domestic catalog only reveals its multipliers after a model refresh. Rather than quietly spending credits on a paid model, testing stays off until one appears — refresh the models, or pick a target model yourself.
en.row.poolTargetStale: The target model you saved is no longer offered: {model}
en.row.poolTargetStaleHint: The region's catalog changed and no longer lists this model, so testing is off rather than running against a model the upstream may not accept. Pick another target, or switch back to automatic.
en.row.probeChannelRejected: ✗ The gateway refused the PROMPT itself, not this account — the opening of a system message matched its third-party-agent filter, so another account or region answers the same way
en.row.probeCredentialRejected: ✗ WorkBuddy refused this account's token — sign in again or pick another account
en.row.probeHint: Send a real-volume request (~25k input tokens) to this model and report whether it answers right now. The upstream rate limit fires on request SIZE — measured: about 20k tokens pass, about 30k are refused — so a small request can look fine while every long-conversation request is refused. This is why every test costs real credits (about 0.7) and runs one model at a time.
en.row.probeModelBusyAt: ✗ This model is loaded right now · not your account; retry after {at}, or switch models
en.row.probeModelBusyUnknown: ✗ This model is loaded right now · not your account — another account will not help; wait about a minute or switch models
en.row.probeNotFound: ✗ The upstream does not know this model
en.row.probeOutOfCreditUnknown: ✗ Not enough credits · the upstream gave no time for when it frees up
en.row.probePolicyRejected: ✗ WorkBuddy's server refused this request under its content policy — re-signing in won't help; try the desktop app or another region/account
en.row.probeRateLimitedUnknown: ✗ Rate limited · the upstream gave no time for when it frees up
en.row.probeUnavailable: ✗ The upstream could not be reached — no usable answer came back
en.row.reloginHint: If errors occur, sign back in to the WorkBuddy app.
en.row.requestFailedHint: Refresh failed — showing the last loaded data: {message}
en.row.rescanHidesKept: The accounts you removed are still hidden: the plugin could not update its own list file. On Windows this is usually a file lock — close antivirus or sync tools that may be holding files in the DSH profile, then try again.
en.row.saveContentionHint: (The file was locked, so the write was refused — on Windows this is usually an antivirus scanner, a sync client such as OneDrive, or an editor with that file open. Close whatever holds it and save again; your edits are still here.)
en.row.searchedHint: If your WorkBuddy keeps its login somewhere else, point the plugin at it with the WORKBUDDY_AUTH_FILE environment variable.
en.row.searchedMore: Show the {count} path(s) that were not found
en.row.selectionLostHint: The saved account no longer exists locally.
en.row.selectionLostMessage: The account saved for this region is no longer among the local sign-ins (WorkBuddy replaced its login or cleaned up backups). Your other sign-ins are fine — pick a current one from the list above. Signing in again in the desktop app will not fix this.
en.row.sessionTitleHint: The host fires one title request per new session and bills it at the main model rate. This re-points that one request at a hidden lightweight model. The request still happens either way. Off by default.
en.row.sessionTitleLabel: Send session titles to the lightweight model
en.row.showCreditsCn: Show credits in the composer toolbar
en.row.showCreditsCnHint: Show the domestic (WB CN) credit balance in the composer toolbar, but only while this session uses a WB CN model. Click it for per-account balances and a one-click test of the checked accounts (the test spends real credits). The readout refreshes by itself every 5 minutes; the per-account table every 60 seconds while it is open.
en.row.showCreditsGlobal: Show credits in the composer toolbar
en.row.showCreditsGlobalHint: Show the international (WB AI) credit balance in the composer toolbar, but only while this session uses a WB AI model. Click it for per-account balances and a one-click test of the checked accounts (the test spends real credits). The readout refreshes by itself every 5 minutes; the per-account table every 60 seconds while it is open.
en.row.showCreditsHintInline: The balance for the account currently serving this tab. Click for per-account balances; it also refreshes every 5 minutes.
en.row.signedOutEncrypted: Your WorkBuddy sign-in is present, but its token fields are encrypted and the plugin could not read the key. Install the WorkBuddy desktop app, or set WORKBUDDY_APP_EXECUTABLE to its executable — signing in again will not change this.
en.row.signedOutHint: Sign in once in the WorkBuddy desktop app; this plugin follows that sign-in automatically.
en.row.signedOutWrongRegion: Your WorkBuddy sign-in was found, but it belongs to the other region tab. Switch tabs above to use it — there is nothing to sign in again.
en.row.tabFreeQuotaWarn: Free models are not unlimited — the upstream limits them by request size and load.
en.row.tabHint: Each tab is a separate provider (workbuddy / workbuddy-global) with its own account, credits, and models. Both sides are live at once: different sessions can pick from either side, and changes on one tab never touch the other.
en.row.tabOffNotice: This provider is switched off: none of its models are offered to DSH. Your account, credits, and model settings are kept — check the box above the tab to bring it back.
en.row.tabSwitchHint: Uncheck to switch this provider off. Its models disappear from the DSH model picker; your account, credits, and model settings are kept and return when you check it again.
en.row.title: WorkBuddy credits & models (dsh-connect-workbuddy)
en.row.tpsHint: Measure this model's output speed: three short requests, median taken. Uses about 256 output tokens per run and costs far less than an availability probe (measured 0.01–0.15 credit). The result is shown with the time it was taken, because speed changes with load and an old number is worse than none.
en.row.tpsNoSample: Could not time this model (too few stream chunks)
en.row.tpsNoUsage: Could not time this model (upstream reported no token count)
en.row.tpsSweepEnabledHint: Measures OUTPUT SPEED for every model you have ENABLED: three runs each, taking the median. Unlike the availability probes above, this sends a tiny prompt and asks for 256 output tokens back, so it costs far less per model (measured 0.01–0.15 credit against 0.72), because this gateway prices by input. Speed matters because DSH dispatches models as parallel sub-agents, so a slow model costs wall-clock time across the whole run.
en.row.transferExportPick: Choose the accounts to export ({total} available):
en.row.transferHint: Move accounts between computers as a JSON file. The file carries the credentials — keep it private. The format is shared with other WorkBuddy credential managers.
en.row.transferImported: Imported {imported} account(s); {skipped} skipped (no token, or belongs to the other region).
en.row.transferPreviewTotal: {total} account(s) in the file — untick what should stay out. Accounts already stored here are overwritten by the import.
en.row.upstreamHint: These change what the gateway sees, not which provider serves the call. All of them are sampled when the plugin mounts, so reload the plugin (or restart DSH) after changing one.
en.row.usageIdentityHint: Adds the X-IDE-* headers (which fill the 使用端 column, otherwise blank) and sends conversation ids as 32-hex UUIDv7. Display alignment only: the User-Agent and the request body never change. Off by default because the evidence comes from a reporter, not from this plugin.
en.row.usageIdentityLabel: Make the usage page record these calls like the official client
en.row.veilHintList: The list refreshes as soon as this finishes.
